April 10, 2025 - Testimony in support of LD 1253:
An Act to Authorize the Commissioner of Marine Resources to Add Limited-access Area Fishing Days
'
During the Scallop Season
Good afternoon Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Marine Resources. Thank you for the opportunity to testify today. My name is
Representative Billy Bob Faulkingham, and I serve as the House Republican Leader. I represent House District 12, which includes the towns of Franklin, Gouldsboro, Hancock, Sorrento, Sullivan, Winter
Harbor, and Steuben. lam here today to testify in support of my bill, LD 1253 -An Act to Authorize
the Commissioner of Marine Resources to Add Limited-Access Area Fishing Days During the Scallop
Season.
This legislation seeks to address the challenges faced by Maine's scallop fishery, which is vital to our
state's economy and specifically our coastal communities. Over the past several years, the fishery has become increasingly volatile, largely due to shifting weather patterns that have led to losses in fishing
days. The short duration ofthe scallop season already limits the ability of fishermen to earn a livelihood, and the unpredictable nature of weather events further exacerbates this challenge, making it harder for our fishermen to maintain sustainable catch.
The scallop season in Maine typically runs from December through April, with limited fishing days. For many of our fishermen, this season represents a crucial window in which they can support their families, invest in their boats and equipment, and contribute to their local communities. However, extreme weather events such as storms, high winds, and rough seas have led to frequent missed
fishing days.
LD 1253 will empower the Commissioner of Marine Resources to add up to five limited-access fishing
days during the scallop season. This flexibility is essential for making up for lost days due to weatherrelated events, and it will help ensure the fishery remains economically viable while also preserving
the sustainability of the scallop population.
By granting the Commissioner the discretion to determine when it is appropriate to add extra fishing days, this bill promotes sustainable fishing practices. If the scallop population is healthy enough to
withstand additional harvest, these extra days will help increase the overall catch without
jeopardizing the long-term health of the fishery. The Maine Department of Marine Resources employs a rigorous, science-based management strategy to safeguard healthy scallop stocks, and this bill would provide the Commissioner the authority to adjust the season as needed based on real-time
conditions.

Maine's scallop fishery is an economic pillar, especially for rural coastal communities where fishing is a primary source of income. LD 1253 provides an opportunity to maximize the economic potential of the fishery during a challenging season, supporting both the livelihoods of fishermen and our broader
coastal communities.
Thank you for your time and consideration. I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.
Respectfully,

TESTIMONY OF
Deirdre Gilbert
Department of Marine Resources
The Department of Marine Resources (DMR) is testifying
in Support of
LD 1253 An Act to Authorize the Commissioner of Marine Resources to Add Limited-access Area
Fishing Days During the Scallop Season Before the Committee on Marine Resources Sponsored by Representative Faulkingham
Date of Hearing: April 10, 2025
Senator Tepler, Representative Hepler, and members of the Joint Standing Committee on Marine
Resources, my name is Deirdre Gilbert, Director of State Marine Policy for the Department of Marine Resources, and l am testifying on behalf of the Department in support of LD 1253.
LD 1253 authorizes the Commissioner of Marine Resources to establish by rule up to 5 limited-access area days during the scallop season if the commissioner determines that additional days are necessary to counteract lost scallop fishing days due to inclement weather or if the scallop population is sufficient to allow additional scallop fishing in those areas.
Maine's scallop fishery is managed through controlling access by the scallop fleet to ensure that the scallop resource remains sufficient to rebuild for future seasons. This is done in a number of ways, including by limiting the number of days in the scallop season, but also by further limiting the number of fishing days in "Limited Access Areas" which may occur only one day per week, as shown in the attached calendar for the 2025 season.
Because the scallop season must be established annually in rule, the specific season days are selected
during the preceding summer, and adopted by the DMR Advisory Council at their fall meeting.
During the 2024 fishing season, poor weather prevented harvesters from utilizing several of the limited access days in Gouldsboro Bay and the Department was contacted to determine if days could be added in consideration of that. Current Department emergency rule-making authority is mainly limited to addressing situations where the resource is at risk of "imminent damage" or "unusual depletion" , so allows the Department to limit, and not expand, opportunity on an emergency basis.
The Department does not object to the potential to expand the number of limited access days if justifiable due to unusually poor weather that would prevent the majority of the fleet from fishing. Realistically this would have to be done through an emergency rule-making process, so the Department recommends that this be achieved by amending the emergency rule-making authorities under Section 6171 Subsection 3, rather than a new section of law, since it would not be possible for the Department to add these days through regular rule-making.
Thank you for your consideration, and I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.
